proposal.thesis: Arista reported ~5 trading days ago (days_since_earnings: 5 on the scan row) and the market's response has been a sustained upward estimate revision, not a fade: 30-day EPS revisions are running +13.4% higher with revision_direction 'up', and forward revenue growth sits at +40.7% (analyst_estimates) -- the Street is raising numbers after the print, not cutting them. On 8/5 the stock broke above its 20-day high (bundle anchored-VWAP anchor at $197.30, breakout_above_20d_high, 2 sessions ago) and has since pulled back to $191.66 today from Friday's $188.67 close -- a -4.4% dip below that breakout level (pct_vs_anchored_vwap -4.4), normal post-earnings digestion inside a fully intact trend: above both 50- and 200-DMA, weekly higher-highs and higher-lows, RSI reset to 58.5 and ADX just 18.6 (not extended). Consensus is strong_buy (recommendation_mean 1.27, n=27) with a $240.04 mean target, 25.3% above Friday's close, and the name screens cheap-vs-growth at a 0.91 forward PEG (fwd_pe_to_growth). I have removed the specific Q2 revenue/guide figures and the individual sell-side target changes from my earlier draft -- those were not in the context bundle and I could not source them -- so this rests on the bundle's revision, valuation, consensus and trend data alone.

proposal.risk_map: The bull case rests on continued upward revisions plus a trend reclaim, both checkable -- if ANET cannot reclaim its $197.30 breakout level within a few weeks, that is a real tell the re-rate stalled, which is exactly what the time-box is for. ANET's demand_driver (networking / datacenter interconnect) sits adjacent to the same hyperscaler-capex complex that hit HPE and DELL hard on 2026-07-15 on 'Meta leasing surplus AI compute' headlines -- a repeat of that narrative would likely drag ANET down even though it carries a different driver label than my HPE position, so I'm watching hyperscaler-capex commentary from MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META as an early tell, not just ANET's own tape. Finally, ANET did not surface in this run's deep-research focus set, so I have no chart, no insider Form 4/5 data, no 13F quarter-over-quarter read, no options-implied move, and -- after removing the unsourced earnings and analyst-target figures -- no bundle news corroboration beyond the numeric scan row itself, which is why I've cut confidence to 0.60.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: the Street is already positioned strong_buy (recommendation_mean 1.27, n=27) with a $240.04 mean target, 25.3% above Friday's close (bundle analyst_ratings), and estimates are being revised up (+13.4% over 30 days). MY VIEW: the equity has not yet caught up to those raised numbers -- it sits 12.2% below its own 52-week high and only marginally above Friday's close, having pulled -4.4% back below its 8/5 breakout level. MECHANISM: heavy pre-print momentum (+33.1% over 3 months, bundle) left the stock exposed to sell-the-news profit-taking right at the print, which is what the pullback below the breakout is -- digestion of an already-strong move, not rejection of the guide, and it is happening while EPS estimates keep being revised UP (+13.4%), which a genuine guide-skepticism scenario would not produce. RESOLUTION: a close back above the $197.30 breakout level within the next ~30 trading days confirms the re-rate toward the raised consensus range; failure to reclaim it within that window is the dated time-box for exiting.
